description.summary: The figure illustrates the MIND framework for zero-shot harmful meme detection, comprising two main modules: 'Similar Sample Retrieval' and 'Insight-Augmented Inference'. The former retrieves similar samples from a reference set using multimodal embeddings, while the latter uses forward and backward prediction with a target sample to derive insights for classification.

components.name: Similar Sample Retrieval
components.description: Retrieves top-K similar samples from the reference set based on embeddings of the target sample.

components.name: Multimodal Embedding
components.description: Combines vision and text encodings into a unified embedding space.

components.name: Vision Encoder
components.description: Processes visual input from the target sample.

components.name: Text Encoder
components.description: Processes textual input from the target sample.

components.name: Insight-Augmented Inference
components.description: Derives insights via forward and backward derivation, then predicts harmfulness using forward/backward predictions and a target sample.

components.name: Forward Derivation
components.description: Generates insight from the samples pool toward the target sample.

components.name: Backward Derivation
components.description: Generates insight from the target sample back to the samples pool.

components.name: Forward Prediction
components.description: Uses forward-derived insight to predict class label.

components.name: Backward Prediction
components.description: Uses backward-derived insight to predict class label.

components.name: Final Prediction
components.description: Combines outputs from forward and backward predictions to produce final classification (e.g., 'Harmful').

metadata.caption: Figure 2: An overview of our proposed framework, MemeCLIP. We use frozen CLIP image and text encoders to create representations for each image-text pair. These representations are passed through linear layers to disentangle the modalities in CLIP's shared embedding space. We implement Feature Adapters with residual connections for each modality to prevent overfitting. We use a cosine classifier to make MemeCLIP more robust to imbalanced data. We initialize classifier weights by using Semantic-Aware Initialization to further improve performance.
metadata.nearby_text: We use frozen CLIP image and text encoders to create representations for each image-text pair. These representations are passed through linear layers to disentangle the modalities in CLIP’s shared embedding space. We implement Feature Adapters with residual connections for each modality to prevent overfitting. We use a cosine classifier to make MemeCLIP more robust to imbalanced data. We initialize classifier weights by using Semantic-Aware Initialization to further improve performance. Inspired by (Gao et al., 2024), we adopt lightweight Feature Adapters for both image and text modalities to learn the features of new data while retaining CLIP’s prior knowl- edge. We further utilize residual connections to integrate prior image and text projections with the outputs of the Adapters, allowing our model to balance the knowledge of the fine-tuned adapter and the disentangled image and text projections. Simi- lar to (Kumar and Nandakumar, 2022), we employ individual linear projection layers for each modal- ity to effectively disentangle image and text repre- sentations in the shared embedding space.
